synopsis: Operator-in-the-loop simulators let a person drive a simulated machine using a cab, screens and controls, enabling studies of warning reaction time, surprise at automatic stops and tolerance of nuisance stops [f16045, f16046]. Because warning-then-brake intervention depends on operator reaction and nuisance interventions are documented as the primary reason deployed proximity systems fail, the booklet recommends an early operator clinic and makes operator acceptance a release criterion [f16053, f16054, f16052, f16056]. For a team starting from zero in October 2026, operator-simulator experiment capability is realistic by mid-2027, conditional on a simulator existing or being procurable [f848]. Named resources include Fraunhofer ITWM RODOS, CM Labs Vortex, Mevea mining simulators, Volvo CE's Simulink/Simscape excavator simulator and an academic haul-truck proximity-interface simulator; Mevea claims over 100 simulator models for more than 50 customers [f16047, f16048, f16049, f16050, f16051, f15964]. The booklet identifies these simulators as a likely need for validation, but the need for warning-then-brake human-factors work remains qualified, and CM Labs' documented use is mainly training rather than collision-mitigation validation [f16055, f9379, f8579, f15968].
